name: MonarchAiCodeBlock
title: AiCodeBlock
summary: Code written by an assistant: MonarchCodeBlock with copy, wrap, diffs and line numbers, plus optional Apply and Insert actions that hand the code back to the app.
whenToUse: For code in an assistant's answer that the person may copy, apply to a file or insert into an editor.
whenNotToUse: For code in documentation or settings that nobody applies, use MonarchCodeBlock. For a short value to copy, use MonarchCopyField.
api: @Composable fun MonarchAiCodeBlock(code: String, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, language: String? = null, title: String? = null, diff: Boolean? = null, highlighted: Boolean = true, showLineNumbers: Boolean = false, showWrapToggle: Boolean = true, copyable: Boolean = true, incomplete: Boolean = false, wrapped: Boolean? = null, onWrappedChange: ((Boolean) -> Unit)? = null, onCopy: ((String) -> Unit)? = null, onInsert: ((String) -> Unit)? = null, onApply: ((String) -> Unit)? = null, labels: MonarchAiCodeBlockLabels = MonarchAiCodeBlockLabels(), actions: (@Composable RowScope.() -> Unit)? = null)

class MonarchAiCodeBlockLabels(apply: String? = null, insert: String? = null, actionLabel: ((action: String, name: String) -> String)? = null, incompleteHint: String? = null, codeBlock: MonarchCodeBlockLabels = MonarchCodeBlockLabels())

options.name: code
options.description: The code, exactly as it should be copied, applied and inserted.

options.name: language
options.description: A language id that picks the highlighter and the header text; "diff" or "patch" turns on the diff mode.

options.name: title
options.description: The header text, such as a file name (the web's filename). It also names the code for TalkBack and the action buttons.

options.name: diff
options.description: Forces the diff mode on or off.

options.name: showLineNumbers
options.description: Line numbers before the lines, not read by TalkBack.

options.name: showWrapToggle
options.description: The wrap toggle in the header.

options.name: copyable
options.description: The copy button in the header.

options.name: incomplete
options.description: The code is still arriving: Apply and Insert are disabled, with a hint saying why. Copy stays available.

options.name: wrapped
options.description: Controls wrapping; without it the block keeps the state itself, starting unwrapped.

options.name: onWrappedChange
options.description: Called with the new wrap state when the toggle is pressed.

options.name: onCopy
options.description: Runs with the copied code after each copy.

options.name: onInsert
options.description: Adds a secondary Insert button that hands over the code.

options.name: onApply
options.description: Adds a primary Apply button that hands over the code.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for Apply, Insert, the spoken action names, the incomplete hint and the code block's own strings.

options.name: actions
options.description: App controls placed in the action row before Insert and Apply.

states.name: ready
states.description: The code block, then a row aligned to the end with the app's controls, Insert (secondary) and Apply (primary).

states.name: incomplete
states.description: Insert and Apply are disabled while the code streams in, and "Available when the code is complete" shows under them; Copy works on what has arrived.

states.name: diff
states.description: Added and removed lines with markers and the diff colors of MonarchCodeBlock.

states.name: no actions
states.description: Without onApply, onInsert or actions there is no action row: the block is a plain MonarchCodeBlock.

appearance: MonarchCodeBlock's subtle container and header, with small buttons under it: Apply in the primary style, Insert in the secondary style, and the hint in the caption style in the muted color. All are theme roles, so light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow.
platformNotes: Same parameters as iOS, with Kotlin names (diff, highlighted, showLineNumbers, showWrapToggle, copyable, incomplete, wrapped with onWrappedChange). On the web Apply and Insert sit in the block's header; MonarchCodeBlock has no slot for extra header controls, so on Android, as on iOS, they are in a row under the code. iOS gives the reason for disabled actions as an accessibility hint; Android has no hint, so the reason is a visible line under the buttons. The web re-tokenises streaming code incrementally; Android re-tokenises the whole code on each update. The web names the header text filename; Android calls it title, as MonarchCodeBlock does. The composable is experimental: an AI panel that waits for a Rook app to adopt it.
accessibility: The code is read as MonarchCodeBlock reads it: a region named after the title or language, line by line, with added and removed lines named.
Apply and Insert are MonarchButtons named with the code, such as "Apply server.ts", with 48dp touch targets.
While the code is incomplete they are disabled and a visible line says "Available when the code is complete".
The action row wraps onto more lines at large font sizes.
edgeCases: Empty code still shows the header and one empty line.
Apply and Insert receive the code as given, including a trailing newline.
With several blocks in one answer, give each a title so the actions are told apart.

examples.title: Filename, line numbers
examples.template:
MonarchAiCodeBlock(
    code = {{code}},
    language = {{language}},
    title = {{filename}},
    showLineNumbers = true,
)

examples.title: A diff that is still streaming
examples.code:
MonarchAiCodeBlock(
    code = "-const port = 3000;\n+const port = 8080;",
    language = "diff",
    incomplete = true,
    onApply = {},
)
